chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from al-Husayn ibn Abi al-'A'la, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the man who sees (in a dream) until he feels desire, so he feels that he has ejaculated, but when he wakes up he does not see the water (semen) in his garment, nor on his body. He (peace be upon him) said: 'There is no ghusl upon him.'

And he (peace be upon him) said: 'Ali (peace be upon him) used to say: 'The ghusl is only due to the great water (discharge). So when he sees in his dream, and does not see the great water, then there is no ghusl upon him.'
ai.seo_question: Is ghusl required if one feels they ejaculated in a dream but finds no semen upon waking?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Kafi* clarifies the distinction between the internal sensation of ejaculation and the external physical evidence required for ritual purity, establishing that ghusl is contingent upon the visible presence of 'the great water' (semen). It reflects the Shia juristic principle of *istishab* (presumption of continuity), where the absence of physical proof negates the obligation of the ritual bath, even if the subjective experience of desire was present. This ruling underscores the practical ease in Shia fiqh, prioritizing tangible signs over mere sensation to avoid unnecessary burden on the believer.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Isa, from Ali Bin Al Hakam, from Al Husayn Bin Abu Al A’ala who said,

‘I asked Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> about the man who sees (a dream) during the sleep until he finds the excitement, so he feels that he has bed-wet. But, when he does wake up, he neither sees the water upon his clothes, nor upon his body. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘The washing is not upon him’.

And he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Ali<sup>asws</sup> was saying: ‘But rather, the washing is due to the great water (discharge). So when he sees in his dream, and does not see the great water (discharge), so a washing is not upon him’.
en.sarwar: 1. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn ‘Isa from Ali ibn al-Hakam from al-Husayn ibn abu al-‘Ala’ who has said the following:

“I once asked abu ’Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about a man who experiences a wet dream and orgasm but when he wakes up, does not find any sign of discharge in his clothes or body. He (the Imam) said, ‘Ghusl (bath) is not necessary on him.

5 He (the Imam) said, ‘Ali, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, would say, “Ghusl (bath) becomes necessary because of major (semen) discharge. If one experiences a wet dream but does not find any sign of semen, Ghusl (bath) is not necessary on him.’””
